utterances.text: I was putting to you what your trial chamber found in relation to your criminal responsibility and I mentioned two things. The disappearance in July 1992 of Burhanudin Kapetanovic and a person by the surname Badnjevic, and then the shooting of at least 50 detainees from the village of Hambarine in late July 1992. And then I put to you that that was the same incident, the shooting of at least 50 detainees, that you referred to in paragraph 38 of your statement where you say that you have no knowledge of it; therefore, it can't be true. Now, is that the same incident that you're referring to, the shooting of the 50 people -- of at least 50 detainees at the end of July?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GRUBAN
utterances.text: Do you want us to discuss Kapetanovic first and then move on, because you linked two completely different and separate incidents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, they are two -- two separate incidents, Mr. Gruban. We can talk about the Kapetanovic incident. Let's look at the circumstances surrounding that. The evidence at your trial from a witness to this incident - and that's Enes Kapetanovic - was that three men including these two, that is, the -- Burhanudin Kapetanovic and the person by the surname of Badnjevic, were roll-called before he was. When Enes got out of the room, you passed by and said: "Stop. Have you been roll-called?" Then you hugged him and told him: "Come here. It would be a pity if such a fellow were gone." Enes stated that later on he heard from his friends that you had said that you had saved him from certain death. Now you said that to Enes Kapetanovic, didn't you? You helped him survive. Didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GRUBAN
utterances.text: People were taken away from Omarska --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Gruban, can you just answer my question, please. You said that to Enes --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GRUBAN
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I cannot answer briefly. If you allow me to describe the circumstances and how this happened, then we will be able to ... will you allow me?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If you answer my question first. You said that to Enes Kapetanovic, didn't you: You helped him survive. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GRUBAN
utterances.text: I helped many people survive all these things, not only him. But, please, let me try to explain the whole situation that led to this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Gruban, the BH Court found that your words and behaviour precisely suggest the uncertainty of the fate of the roll-called detainees, and it led the court to the conclusion that the detainees were supposed to be liquidated. Now, you knew that people were being called out, in particular, on the night shifts, and they were not returning.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GRUBAN
utterances.text: Not true. I didn't know what happened to people who left the centre. There were many roll-calls and people separated, and fortunately, there are many people among those who were taken away and who survived. Unfortunately, there were cases when people were taken away, and, regrettably, they are no longer alive. So we cannot generalise and say that everybody who was called out is dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So you --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GRUBAN
utterances.text: There were people taken out, transfers to Trnopolje, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So you were aware of all these roll-calls?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GRUBAN
utterances.text: I couldn't know about all of them. I knew about some and I can talk about those that I was aware of. But if you allow me, I can describe to you the Kapetanovic case as it really happened. And Enes himself testified that I didn't know that those other people had been called out before him, and I did ask him: "Were you called out?" And while I was in the duty officer room, I didn't hear that there would be any roll-calls or people taken away that same night. I asked him if he was hungry. I offered to take him to the kitchen to find some bread. There was no bread. I got him back into his room. In the meantime, I went to the stairs and met the driver of the SUP Prijedor. I heard that two persons had been taken away in the meantime. I didn't ask where they were going. And I told Mejakic that I had put Enes back in his room and Mejakic said, "Never mind." So Enes remained. And there is no example that any guard would make any inquiries as to who is going where. Other made people made decisions as to who is going where. The guards are there to make sure that everybody is treated the same way, to protect everyone, and whenever there are transfers, categorisations, sending people someplace, that's other people's job. Just like your guards here do not ask who is going where, and that's normal. If they did ask such questions --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 101, line 16. The witness said: People were taken out, transfers to Trnopolje, people released to go home, and that last part is not recorded. We can listen to the tape, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Gruban? Did you say so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can also give examples of people who were released to go home, who left later with inspectors --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I simply asked whether you confirmed with Mr. Karadzic. Please continue, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So, in relation to people being called out at night-time, you were happy for this to happen. You were -- you were there, it was your job to provide security for the detainees, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GRUBAN
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Every guard was to supposed to look after the security of prisoners. However, if you get a list of persons whom you are asked to let go with someone else, then have you no right to ask questions, who, what, why, you just turn these people over.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And who was giving you these lists?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GRUBAN
utterances.text: The lists were usually brought by drivers who came to fetch those people. The list would be typed up and signed, and the people were supposed to be turned over, according to the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Signed by who?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GRUBAN
utterances.text: The list was signed by the chief of the public security station. Without his approval and consent, nobody could leave the collection and investigation centre. In the early days - and the whole thing was meant to last very -- a very short time - it happened that when people were interrogated and inspectors established that these people had not been part of the insurgency, had not committed crimes, people were released immediately. Later it was forbidden to release them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Gruban, I want you to concentrate on the people that were getting called out and taken away and never to be seen again. You knew that people were being taken away and you continued to allow these things to happen?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GRUBAN
utterances.text: Not correct. Not correct. I didn't know where people were being taken. Many of my friends who were incarcerated were asking me whether I could put them on the list to be called up to go home. I'm telling you, there were people who were transferred and who are still alive. On the other hand, there were people who were called, who were taken away, and, unfortunately, are no longer among us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. Now you heard Enes Kapetanovic give evidence in your trial in Bosnia. And it's true that he stated that later on he heard from a detainee -- he heard from his friends that you had said that you had saved him from a certain death; correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GRUBAN
utterances.text: He stated that before the court. I still meet him every now and then. We greet each other. We socialise. If he thought that I had done something wrong or bad, I'm sure that we wouldn't talk today. He is absolutely aware what my role was, what my power was. He knew that I was powerless. It was just a lucky coincidence that I saved him on that day. I didn't know anything about the roll-calls at the time. And that's the long and the short of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll continue tomorrow morning. Mr. Gruban, I'd like to advise you not to discuss with anybody else about your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 20th day of February, 2014, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.47 p.m.,
